newsitem.title: USA: MGM Grand plans aggressive move in Detroit.
newsitem.headline: MGM Grand plans aggressive move in Detroit.

text.p: Leo the Lion, world famous trademark of MGM film studios and an icon of the MGM Grand hotel in Las Vegas, may soon roar into Detroit as part of a newly approved gambling law in that city.

In November, Detroit voters passed a law that calls for three gambling licenses there, making it one of the first major markets to open in years. And MGM Grand Inc. is ready to pounce on one of those licenses.
"We intend to be aggressive bidders," MGM President Alex Yemenidjian said in a recent interview.

Following the opening of the New York, New York hotel Jan. 3 here, MGM Grand has a full slate of projects for 1997. It will continue revamping the MGM Grand hotel, finalising plans for a hotel/casino in Atlantic City and expanding a joint venture in South Africa.

But winning a license in Detroit is high on MGM Grand's list. Yemenidjian said an MGM Grand hotel/casino would likely take 24 to 30 months to complete once a plans are drawn up, adding the licensing process may start as early as April.
Detroit officials were not immediately available to comment.
Though it is too early for details, any Detroit operation would be built in the grand style for which MGM Grand is known.

New York, New York, which has a facade that replicates the Manhattan skyline with copies of the Empire State, Chrysler and other buildings, opened to crowds lined up on the sidewalks and streets outside.
Yemenidjian said MGM Grand was very pleased with the opening, and "every single day has exceeded expectations" in terms of casino traffic and game play.

The interior, which had been shrouded in secrecy, is designed like different parts of Manhattan. Its high ceilings, fountains and subdued lighting give the affect of strolling along city streets, albeit among ringing slot machines.
Various bands play in the open atmosphere and several restaurants, bars and a discotheque are tucked into building fronts that look like uptown brownstones or downtown offices.
"It's going to be a real driver of demand at the south end of the Strip," said David Wolfe, financial analyst at Oppenheimer & Co.
Six months after the opening, MGM Grand or its 50-percent partner, Primadonna Resorts Inc. can acquire the other company's share in New York, New York.
Currently, however, the partnership works well, and the companies are pleased with the arrangement, Yemenidjian said.
He declined comment on whether MGM Grand has talked to Primadonna about a possible merger of the two companies.

"We will probably have most of our growth through construction of new properties instead of acquisitions," he said. "But it would be a mistake to rule out the possibility of an acquisition, whether that's Primadonna or (others)."

Meanwhile, the revamping of the MGM Grand hotel into a "City of Entertainment" continues. A transformation of the food court is nearly complete, and soon the company will begin tearing down the lion head at the entryway to replace it with a fountain and statue of Leo.

The hotel's theme park will be trimmed from 33 acres to 18 acres to accommodate an entertainment and retail centre. MGM Grand may build an area like Walt Disney World's "Pleasure Island", which is filled with restaurants and bars, in the entertainment centre, Yemenidjian said.
Talk in financial markets is that the cost of construction may rise to $300 million from the previously planned $250 million.
"We haven't officially changed the numbers," Yemenidjian said. "It's possible it could cost more, but if it does it would be because ... the returns are justifiable."
He gave "a better than even chance" the company will be able to obtain the land it needs to begin groundbreaking for a new hotel/casino in Atlantic City by late 1997.

Synergies with MGM film studio, which is controlled by MGM Grand majority shareholder Kirk Kerkorian, include advertising on a recently launched cable TV channel in Asia, a possible daily talk show from the MGM Grand and filming a James Bond movie on location in Las Vegas.
